quest.title: The Splendorous Sky That Day
quest.description: To solve the anomaly that has appeared in the sky, you must first go into the desert to make contact with the "Nagarjunites"...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x25000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Found it, found it! Paimon wonders what it is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Aw, come on, this is no treasure. It's just some tattered old drum!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't know what it could be used for, either.

choices.text: If we brought this to Royinjan the antique seller...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that's right. Despite its rather shabby appearance, it might still be some valuable antique!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We might be able to sell it for a good price at Royinjan's, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, hold on. There's a note over there at the side. It might just hold some clues!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see... Huh. This seems to have been left by an adventurer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "The Sign of Apaosha"... Uh, Paimon's not super sure what this guy's talking about, but he sure is irresponsible, leaving a commission unfinished just because it's hard!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But since that's how things are, let's hand this drum over to Katheryne and let her reassign someone to complete... whatever commission this was.

choices.text: If we brought this one back to the Akademiya...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, they might want to hear more about something we found in the desert.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's not all that interested in this studying stuff, but if we can make a little this and that off their budget, why not, right?

choices.text: Let's say we brought this back to the Grand Bazaar...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! Maybe the people at the Theater could make use of this. But wouldn't they already have a lot of these instruments there already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But y'know, it's not as if Paimon really knows the difference between drum types or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #Hello there, {NICKNAME}. How have your recent travels gone?

choices.text: They've gone quite well, thank you.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I've heard about your previous adventures. It seems that you've become very experienced.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: As long as you keep going, I believe that it will only be a matter of time before you become a truly great adventurer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, speaking of adventures, we found this on one of ours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This was left by some irresponsible adventurer. We thought it'd be bad if the commission he took never got resolved, so we brought it back here.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hmm... Indeed, this item is key to a particular commission. Thank you very much.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The commission linked to this drum is a very important one from the Akademiya and is also critical to the expansion of our operations.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Unfortunately, though we have previously given this commission to various talented adventurers, they have all invariably failed.

choices.text: A commission from the Akademiya...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Well, this is an issue that even the Akademiya cannot solve, so we did expect a relatively high failure rate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Actually, Paimon's getting kinda curious now. What sorta commission is this anyway?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Simply put, a recent star observation by researchers from the Akademiya led to the discovery that the northern skies have become blocked by a strange, heretofore unseen phenomenon.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Concerned that this would have a great impact on the accuracy of any astrological calculations, the Akademiya immediately put people together to investigate.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: This resulted in them delving into ancient records, within which they found mention of a strange phenomenon known as the Sign of Apaosha, which bears strong similarities to the recent occurrence.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: According to these records, this celestial sign appeared after the disaster that engulfed most of Teyvat five hundred years ago.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Although the circumstances of its eventual disappearance are unclear, its position has been determined to be near the Temir Mountains, at the northernmost regions of the desert.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: However, that area has only ever been sparsely populated. Even when the ancient desert realms were at their peak, they did not extend that far.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: And after the cataclysm five hundred years ago, that place was one of the areas worst affected by the encroaching Abyss due to it being connected to an ancient underground realm.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Since then, it has been declared a restricted zone by the Akademiya. The only people who still live there are a mysterious Darshan known by the Akademiya as the Nagarjunites.

choices.text: Huh. A mysterious Darshan, you say.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If even you're calling it mysterious, Katheryne, it's gotta be something super mysterious...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Though they seem like legends to the average person, they were once a Darshan of the Akademiya, albeit one that split off five hundred years ago.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Then, the researchers who wished to fight the monsters from the Abyss banded together and traveled to the depths of the desert, and the Nagarjunites are an organization comprised of the people who stayed there in the end.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: That said, it has been many years since, and they have branched off further and further from the Akademiya. They even seem to have developed their own academic traditions.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: It seems that they also worship a form of energy known as Khvarena. This energy communicates with them in the form of spirits... Well, I feel that I'm going off-topic now.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: The Akademiya believes that this faction is strongly related to this celestial sign. However, they have not been able to establish contact with this group and, as such, have commissioned the Guild to assist in their investigations.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: This is a win-win situation for us as well. Ruins related to Khaenri'ah are located nearby, but exploration in that area has been declared taboo by the Akademiya until now.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: If this commission is a success, perhaps we will be able to participate in future expeditions to those ruins.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Since you have heard me say this much, why don't you take this commission on?

choices.text: You're just finding someone to step up to the plate, huh?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Hardly. It is following careful analysis that I have found you best suited to this task. After all, your pioneering spirit is something rare even amongst adventurers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So after all that, it sounds like we just need to look for those Whateverites, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like it'll be pretty easy! And we'll get some Mora from the Akademiya, too...

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Yes. That drum you picked up was originally given to us by the Akademiya to be used as a token of good faith in our dealings with the Nagarjunites.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: Just give it to the organization's leader. It stands to reason that they will have some way to solve this problem.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: I'll be leaving this task in your hands, then. I've marked the rough position of the Temir Mountains for you. Ad astra abyssosque, Traveler! May you inscribe a new legend in the desert sands.

choices.text: Guess this is our business now, huh?

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: After some careful analysis, I believe that you are best suited to this task. After all, your pioneering spirit is something rare even amongst adventurers.

choices.text: Well, since Khaenri'ah is involved...
The Nagarjunites...?
Oh boy, here comes trouble.
It's been a little tiring.

response.speaker: Katheryne
response.text: It would not hurt to take a little rest from time to time.

talks.objective: Talk to the person near the camp

dialogues.text: Who are you?
You guys don't look like tribespeople of the desert, more like adventurers from a faraway land.
...But no matter who you are, this is as far as you will get. Please go back.

choices.text: We've been commissioned to come here.

response.text: Commission? What commission? As far as I know, the Akademiya of the rainforest has declared this area a restricted zone. Why would there be commissions?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We were commissioned to investigate something up in the sky that looks like bad news! The Sign of... what was it again?
"The Sign of Apaosha."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, yep! That's the one!
...Wait. How did you come to know its name?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Katheryne of the Adventurers' Guild told us! ... Hang on a minute. Didn't you mention the correct name just now?
Since you know of "The Sign of Apaosha," you must have heard of us "Shama{RUBY#[D]Order of Skeptics}niyya," right?
The desert past this point is a restricted zone under our guard. As a Ranger of the Order of Skeptics, I cannot let you pass, no matter what reason you may have.

choices.text: The Order of Skeptics?

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: My apologies, I forgot to introduce myself. I'm Pyrrho, a member of the Order of Skeptics in charge of guarding this place.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Order of Skeptics"? Paimon remembers that Katheryne told us to look for the "Nagarjuicites" or something. Umm, looks like Pyrrho isn't the one we're looking for...

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: "Nagarjunites"? Hmph. That's just a derogatory name that those guys from the rainforest have for us!

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Lord Nagarjuna is a hero who fought against the "De{RUBY#[S]monster}v" alongside the divine bird's heirs. He gained divine power through the "Rite of Chinvat" and put an end to the calamity.

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: How dare they call such a great hero — and our first Vijnanapati — by his given name!

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Wait, why am I telling you outsiders this? Are... are you two spies from the Akademiya?

choices.text: We're here to take care of a problem.

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Aha! So you are the Akademiya's henchmen! We've tried our best to keep a low profile, but still, you've managed to find our trail...

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Still, I'd believed that the Akademiya was full of cowards who would never dare to step foot into the desert. I won't lie — you've impressed me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon didn't expect you to have such a strong opinion about the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Of course! Lord Nasu{RUBY#[S]Vijnanapati}raia has said that we wouldn't have been reduced to this state if it weren't for them.

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: ...Wait. So you are here to gather intelligence after all! Ugh, I've revealed more than I should... Anyway, please leave. If this conversation continues...

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: As unwilling as I might be to do so, I would have to end you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? You're the one who couldn't resist blabbing. Why are you putting the blame onto us?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Also, there's no need to be rash... Oh right, {NICKNAME}, show Pyrrho the token that Katheryne gave us. He'll know what's going on once he sees it!

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Token? This had better not be some trick!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ta-da！Look, told you we weren't lying!

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: What is this shabby drum... You call this a token?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Did Katheryne mix things up?

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: You guys don't think you can bribe me with such a small thing, do you? Leave now, or things will get nasty.

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Don't you underestimate us Skeptics!

choices.text: Spare us!

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: It's too late to beg for mercy!

choices.text: Bring it on!
We're here because we accepted a commission from the Akademiya...

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Hmph. So, the Akademiya folks have been reduced to hiring some no-name adventurers to do their dirty work, eh? Cowards, just as I thought!

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: I thought they might send some mercenaries over at the worst. What an oversight on my part...

choices.text: Ranger?
We are here to resolve the issue regarding the Sign of Apaosha.

response.text: "The Sign of Apaosha"... How did you know of this name?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We are adventurers who have an organization at our backs. Katheryne of the Adventurers' Guild told us, of course!

dialogues.text: Cease! Cease, I say!

dialogues.speaker: Pyrrho
dialogues.text: Lady Sorush... Why did you... You didn't have to attend to such trivial matters personally, let alone in front of these outsiders...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: We Pari appear before whoever we wish, and our volition is not for you mere mortals to question. How dare you overstep your bounds!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (This little thing is about Paimon's size, and the way she talks is kind of funny... Why's Pyrrho calling "Lady" in that reverent tone?)

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmph, your sins will be judged, but the time for that has yet to come. The two of you over there, as envoys of the Akademiya, it is only polite to state your names first, no?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, we should have introduced ourselves first, but that high-and-mighty attitude of yours is...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: My words and actions are not contrary to traditions and principles of the Pari. The same cannot be said for you nameless persons... Hmph.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Ugh... Fine! We're not nameless. Paimon is Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. We're adventurers who came here on a commission.

choices.text: I'm the one who is an adventurer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! We adventure together all the time!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I need only know your names. Your other trivialities do not concern me. However, as for that drum...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: #That item has a profound connection with us Pari, and is not something that you mortals should possess. {NICKNAME}, I command you to present it to me immediately.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: No way! At least sound nicer about it when you're asking someone for a favor!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Besides, this item is important to our commission. We're to hand it to the leader of this Order of yours.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we give it to you and fail to complete the commission because of that, not only might we lose our reward, we might even have to pay Mora to the Adventurers' Guild! That's a huge loss!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Reward? Mora? To think that you would risk your lives in a place fraught with peril for such frivolous reasons... You know nothing of what transpires here.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: One mistake would send your race tumbling into an eternal samsara, and yet you commit deeds that are beyond even our comprehension.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: You humans are such... interesting beings.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: No matter... I shall bring you to the "leader" you speak of. This item would remain worthy tribute even if you should only present it to me after that meeting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's more like it... Wait, that's still not right! We still have to deal with that huge hole in the sky! And if we don't...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: ...Huge hole? You refer to the Sign of Apaosha, then? And you wish to quell this calamity with mere mortal coils?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hah, how presumptuous! It is the duty of us Pari to eradicate the Sign of Apaosha — an endeavor that I, Sorush, shall give my all to accomplish!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: To quell this calamity, I must follow in the footsteps of the divine bird Simurgh, and sacrifice everything that one might call "Sorush"...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: To stand in my way is not a sin that one such as you may bear!

choices.text: Simurgh?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Foolish beings, have you not heard of the divine bird Simurgh? She is the master of Khvarena who once saved the land from destruction.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Legend has it that it was she who split into infinite motes of Khvarena after her sacrifice, thus quelling the catastrophe.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, sure, but Paimon doesn't think that we'll need you to sacrifice yourself...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph. In any case, this matter is far beyond your capabilities, and your intervention is futile... All you must do is bear silent witness as I transcend.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: You shall receive remuneration from this Guild of yours so long as the calamity is quelled, will you not?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Still, do not forget to extol my virtues and laud my accomplishments. After all, even the greatest heroes shall require mere mortals like you to sing of their deeds.

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: But Lady Sorush, the Vijnanapati has instructed us to forbid suspicious individuals from interfering before the ritual is completed...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I have decided, and as a Pari, my word is law!

response.speaker: Pyrrho
response.text: Umm...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Alright, follow me. I shall take you to the "leader" you spoke of.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But gird yourselves all the same. That which lies ahead is not a place that human beings can easily set foot in.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: If you get lost or end up being eaten by some monster appearing out of nowhere, there shall be nothing I can do for you.

choices.text: Huh...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Umm, Paimon doesn't think that we'll need you to sacrifice yourself for this, though...

choices.text: We are here to look for the Order of Skeptics.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What do you mean, "Dev"? Aren't these just Abyss Mages and hilichurls?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: To think you would so easily defeat the rampaging Dev. Your strength is most radiant indeed. Consider me impressed.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Though there is still quite the gap between you and us Pari, the sight of you fighting valiantly reminds me of those humans of legend who once fought alongside us.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I have decided, then. You shall have the honor of being my Yasnapati!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yasnapati? Paimon doesn't know what that is, but coming from you, it can't be anything good, really.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Do you not have such things amongst humans? Strategists, scribes, and the like? Those who exist to praise the heroes whose stories they exist in?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Neither of those jobs are what you just described!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: No matter how great the hero, their great deeds must be recorded and sung of by others. If not, the same fate that befell ancient heroes shall befall them also...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Though they may have loved violence and conflict, great deeds are still great deeds, and they deserved to be remembered.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: *sigh* Alas, those who loved conflict would be consumed by it, and once they had slain each other, they were all lost.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: And because there were no authors or poets to tell of their deeds, once all who had lived in such times were gone, their works forgotten to the last. I will not be like them.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: My great work shall shine so gloriously that the world itself will suffer great loss to not know of it. Thus, I shall now give you permission to record those deeds...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Rejoice and give thanks, for is this not a grace that few receive from us Pari?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This all sounds very complicated, but basically, you just need someone to tell you how awesome you are, right?

choices.text: Not interested, thanks.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! There's nothing worth bragging about with you. You just look kinda cute, that's all.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Your refusal is futile. Orders given by a Pari are absolute!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: And what do you mean, cute? I am valiant! Heroic!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Whatever the case, it has been decided. Fret not, you shall be free to do as you please once I have sacrificed myself to restore the pure skies.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Till then, you shall witness my valiant form!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, sure, even if Paimon can't see it...

choices.text: Sounds like an alright gig.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, what are you talking about! Paimon doesn't consent to this!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Well, you are quite bright, aren't you? As I would expect of someone I have my eye on.

choices.text: Couldn't you find a Skeptic to help you out there?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The Skeptics? I may admire their spirit, but other than their leader, whom you mentioned previously, the rest are not fit for such work.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: They speak all day of how conflict is the true nature of this world, but they have themselves lost all ability to engage in such.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: None of them will be able to witness my sacrifice to its end.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The path here is now dotted with Gray Crystals. When I last left it, it was not yet so.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gray Crystals? You mean the crystals we're seeing everywhere?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's had her eye on them for a while now. What are they?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Gray Crystals are remnants of the black fire's embers. Proof that this land has suffered great calamity.

choices.text: The black fire...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Indeed. I am sure you have heard that a great catastrophe struck long ago, where dark fire rose from beneath the earth and scorched the land.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The dark fire opened a bottomless hollow in this land, and the demons of Dev that crawled through that gap nearly turned this into a lightless realm.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Though the gap was blocked by the great tree, the dark fire's filth spread like seeds, and the countless dark and painful memories, released by that corruption, began to lay down roots and sprout.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: This persisted till the honored lord of Khvarena, the divine bird Simurgh, drank the primordial water left behind by our god, before transforming herself into Khvarena of all kinds and scattering across the land.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: From that day on, the Khvarena has taken the divine bird's place in defending this land, and those painful memories that leaked out have been sealed by Khvarena.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: What was left are these ubiquitous Gray Crystals. Though they seem no different from any other stone, they may contain objects that are yet to be purified.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: The Gray Crystals in the area have increased of late. I suspect that this must have something to do with the Sign of Apaosha's dark power.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But if we use Khvarena's might, we can get rid of these crystals.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: If my senses do not deceive me, a wandering Khvarena should be nearby. Let us look around.

choices.text: The calamity...

talks.objective: Use the power of Khvarena to destroy the Gray Crystals
Go to the training grounds of the Order of Skeptics
Talk to the leader of the Skeptics

dialogues.text: Lady Sorush, Khvarena's Envoy, you have returned.
Though it has taken much work on my part, the analysis of documents regarding the Rite of Chinvat will soon be complete.
According to my research, we need only collect all the Great Songs of Khvarena next, and your great work may then be completed.
Wait a moment. You two are...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #Do not fret. They are {NICKNAME} and Paimon, my newly-chosen Yasnapati and {M#his}{F#her} companion. They are here to witness my great work.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey now, Paimon hasn't agreed to that yet!
A Yasnapati, you say... Though I will not question your most astute judgment, I fear that allowing ignorant outsiders into this land before the Rite of Chinvat is complete may have untoward effects.
Know that the people of the Akademiya surely do not desire the Rite's completion.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Speak no further. I have my reasons for doing this.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: #Well, then. Take that drum from before out, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You bring the drum out, as agreed.
A Koryb{RUBY#[S]drum}antes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A Korybantes, you say?
Hahaha! Yes. This is an important catalyst for the ritual needed to forge a Lau{RUBY#[S]connection}pa between ourselves and the Pari.
I have searched for many years for this, and to think it now comes to me! Ah, this is indeed a good omen for my future plans.
It would be good if the fates will also be with me when I lead the Order of Skeptics to throw down the Akademiya and burn their House of Daena, or whatever they call it, to the ground.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow. What a way to casually paint yourself as the villain, huh?
Villain? Hah! The Akademiya are the true villains here, have no doubt of that!

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Ah, I forgot my introductions. I am Nasejuna, the Vijnanapati of the Order of Skeptics, we who cultivate ourselves here. If you would use the terminology of the Akademiya, I would be the equivalent of a "sage."

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: But I doubt those pampered folk would care much for what we at the margins call ourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: You do not look much like those the Akademiya might send.

choices.text: We're just passing adventurers.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Fair enough, though in truth it would not matter even if you were to be from that dratted place.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Even if the entire Corps of Thirty were to be sent here, my plans could not be halted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, whatever your plans are, we didn't come here to stop them, that's for sure.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Hah! So they would all say, those treacherous louts from the Akademiya. And when my guard is down, you would stab me in the back!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Just like those people in funny masks who try to skulk about and steal our academic tomes.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: They even dared to attack our honored envoy of Khvarena, Lady Sorush!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmph. And they met defeat at my hands, each one of them!

choices.text: Very impressive, Sorush.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Of course, my Yasnapati. It is right that you should sing my praises!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Do not look upon us as some miserable few who inhabit the Temir Mountains! We once had such numbers that all the desert north of Mt. Damavand would struggle to hold us.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: It is only because of our harsh environment and the slander and ostracism by the Akademiya that we have been reduced to this.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: If it was not for such sage souls as myself holding things together and the protection of Khvarena, we Skeptics would have been reduced to nothing long ago.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like quite the disagreement, yes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Katheryne said that you have your differences, but it sure looks to Paimon like you Skeptics really hate the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Say not "hate," but rather that we simply cannot coexist.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: When I was young, I did go there to learn in an attempt to mend our differences, but they treated me like an outsider.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Though they feign politeness by calling us a branch of the Akademiya, this is naught but a means to belittle us!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: It is said that our predecessors had a clash of ideals with them, and so chose to go into the desert to stand against the darkness themselves.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: From that day on, we have been holding firm in the war against defilement, defending our land, and what have those useless louses been doing in the meantime?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Compared to those pampered pedants, we who combine thought, word, and deed far better deserve honor for our wisdom!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, Paimon doesn't quite get it...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: You need only understand that conflict is the true nature of this world.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Khvarena and impurity, Dahri and the true way... It is these struggles for supremacy that have kept this world alive, just as surely as this sky does.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Those sophists in their fancy Darshans believe that the fates of all are inscribed in the skies, and that this is the supreme wisdom and truth.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: But look! The skies reflect defilement itself! Surely their "truth," then, is an imperfect thing.

choices.text: Perhaps nothing is truly perfect.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Ah, think you thus? Then we might yet be friends. If time permits, we may discuss this issue in more detail.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Nasuraia. This is not the time to talk about such things. Have you not seen how the Gray Crystals hem us in ever more tightly?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: If we do not extinguish the Sign of Apaosha soon, things shall grow most perilous indeed...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, speaking of the Sign...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right! That's right! We were tasked to fix this... hole thing. But after all this talking, we still don't know what it's supposed to be!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Ha. Well, our plans also involve extinguishing that celestial mark. As for what it is... If it must be described as anything, let us call it the water's surface.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The water's surface? Your explanation's just making things more confusing...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: The water's reflection, while an illusion, nonetheless hides the truth within itself. So it is with the skies. It is like a mirage, if you have seen those before.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, that big hole up there is way spookier than any mirage!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Well, it should be, for that celestial sign reflects an otherworldly hellscape!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Long, long ago, Dah{RUBY#[S]Khaenri'ah}ri once built a facility here that connected them to realms beyond.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: During the great disaster, which they say the Dahri started, monsters swarmed from that very facility into the nations of the world.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: The monsters tore open a great rift that came to be called the Tunigi Hollow, and though they were sealed away with the new vein of the ancient tree, this mysterious sign appeared along with that.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: What the sign reflects is that which lies beyond the dark rift, and though the monsters cannot enter Teyvat through that illusion, it nonetheless radiates corrupt energies.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: They say that our very first Vijnanapati extinguished that strange sign together with the Pari, but as the power of impurity has strengthened over time, this ancient symbol has appeared once more.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: And should we leave it be... Who knows? That hollow may truly re-emerge one day, and that ancient war will be reenacted. In truth, it might be interesting to live in such exciting times.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? No! That wouldn't be interesting at all!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: It matters not. Simurgh drank the Amrita left behind by our god, transmuting herself into limitless Khvarena.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: As the heirs to the divine bird, solving this problem is the mission that we Pari have. I, Sorush, will surely leave behind a work great enough to be her equal.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Of course, of course, Khvarena's Envoy. And we of the Order of Skeptics shall surely help you see your duty through.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh. What's with all this talk about "sacrifice"? Is that really necessary to solve this problem?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Well... In truth, I do not know. All documents regarding the Sign of Apaosha have long been lost, and the traditions and rites surrounding it have also ceased to be passed down.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: If it had not been for me constantly looking up what documents were left, there might not have been anymore left to know that the Rite of Chinvat existed at all.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: According to my research, the Pari are the descendants of Simurgh, and should therefore also have the power to transform into Khvarena to purify the land.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: And would you not say that a grand sacrifice to save the world on the part of the divine bird's heirs very much suits our Order's style?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? That's so... haphazard! This sacrifice you're talking about doesn't sound like a small thing either... Why aren't we thinking of other ways to solve this issue?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon's sure there's gotta be some alternative, right, {NICKNAME}? It's always been this way, hasn't it?

choices.text: Yup.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I already said that you need not interfere. Simply witnessing my sacrifice shall suffice.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: It is something worth celebrating that we Pari should sacrifice our lives to purify the earth.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, you say that, but...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: I would ask that you keep a respectful distance from that which you do not comprehend, outsiders.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: But since this is the case... Well, I was planning to investigate the Tunigi Hollow to make preparations for the Rite of Chinvat anyway.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Why don't you come along? I trust that you also wish to see the scars left behind by a fissure that once led beyond our world's bounds.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: When you see it, I believe you shall understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon is kinda curious...

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: A sound plan. In that case, I shall lead the way. After all, you would find it impossible to freely traverse this land where Khvarena battles against impurity.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: My Yasnapati, follow me to the end. Watch me complete my mission!

choices.text: I am very good at my job, after all.
This logic seems a tad messy...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Only those who dare to refute the "truth" can gain true wisdom. It seems that such courage is not found in you.

choices.text: I'm guessing those were the Fatui?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: The Fatui? I know not of what you speak, but they were city-folk, so I doubt the Akademiya would be far behind in the shadows.

choices.text: We did take a commission from them, sure...

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: And so you are of them, after all. But it matters not.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Is that deep pit the Tunigi Hollow you were talking about earlier?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's super huge crystals all over the place, even bigger than the ones we saw before! They look scarier, too...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: These were once huge trees used to seal and subdue the creatures of the dark depths. The power of defilement has corrupted them, warping them into such forms as you see now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Since the monsters have been sealed, it sure doesn't look like anyone needs to sacrifice themselves again.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: That is why we must use the power of Khvarena to re-open the way...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey! Wouldn't that just release the monsters again? They took so much effort to seal, too!

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: No, no... I mean that we must open the path to the Sign of Apaosha. The way to the rift in the earth was sealed long ago. It can never lead to the true darkness again.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: But that is exactly why that sealed rift does indeed connect to the illusion of the abyss.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: We need only use the Great Songs of Khvarena to stabilize the seal before initiating the Rite of Chinvat to pass through the darkness and reach the Sign.

choices.text: The Great Songs of Khvarena?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: They are the mightiest manifestations of the Khvarena scattered throughout the world. We can use the Great Songs to initiate the Rite of Chinvat.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: After that, we can open up a path to the darkness, just as legend holds that the first Vijnanapati Nagarjuna and the Pari did.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's all well and good, but what will we do once we reach the side that the Sign is on?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: I do not know what happens after that. I have encountered legends that our first Vijnanapati Nagarjuna was lifted up to the heavens, where he used divine power to extinguish the sign, but that, I feel, is mere myth.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: I believe that Khvarena's Envoys will have some way. Since they can purify the defiling impurities, they must also have some way to extinguish the Sign.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Hah, did Sorush not also say that she wishes to imitate the sacrifice of Simurgh? The world is built upon conflict and sacrifice, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well that's what Sorush says, sure, but that's... that's way too irresponsible of you!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Oh, don't fret. Before the necessity of any sacrifice can be ascertained, we must still bring the Great Songs of Khvarena together. At the moment, we have yet to take even the first step forward.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-huh, says the guy who's just been talking this whole time.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Well... Basically, only the Pari who has been chosen as a Bloomguard can touch the Great Songs.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: But our current Envoy, Lady Sorush, has yet to obtain that right.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is that so? For all that bluster, you really aren't all that, huh, Sorush?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: You dare speak to me like that, Pale Floater?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, Paimon isn't a Pale Floater!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Only by obtaining the Twin-Horned Chaplet may she become the Bloomguard, a being able to gather the power of Khvarena. As such, she must first be acknowledged by Lady Zurvan, the First Pari.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: She is a mighty Pari who once fought alongside our ancestors. It is even said that she was the very Pari who fought alongside the ancient heroes to subdue the embers of the Abyss.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But that elder of ours is... utterly unreasonable. She refuses to acknowledge my dearest desire. I'm afraid there's nothing I can do about that.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Still, even without the Twin-Horned Chaplet, my sacrifice will suffice to accomplish this deed.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Of course, I do not intend to doubt your desire to sacrifice yourself this way, but if you are unable to perform the Rite and pass through the dark hollow, your wish will not be fulfilled nonetheless.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: However, I do have a suggestion. Lady Sorush called you her Yasnapati, did she not?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Why don't you go with her to the Vourukasha Oasis? That is where Lady Zurvan may be found.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Perhaps Lady Zurvan may yet change her mind should she see that we humans view Lady Sorush as the predestined envoy.

choices.text: And why aren't you going?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Well, as for me... She would certainly look down on a bookish man like me, considering her many years of experience.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: If she looked upon me, I doubt she would ever change her mind again. Haha!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: This is the only method we have at present to change our current situation, so please, do go with Lady Sorush to the sacred place protected by the Khvarena...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph, aren't you a sneaky one? Looks like you're the only person coincidentally out of a job!

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Of course not! There is much I must do. For example... The preparations for the Rite of Chinvat still must be done.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: I must also consult the words of the ancient scribes once more to ascertain the locations of the Great Songs.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: As for the Kory Drum you brought, I believe I may now form a connection once more with the Pari who still remain in slumber.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Their awakening is necessary for the Rite of Chinvat to occur.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: Regardless, I leave the matter of the Twin-Horned Chaplet to you two. Once everything is complete, let us meet at the campsite upon the Temir Mountains.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh well. So we have to look for that Pari elder, right? Well, let's hope she isn't as nasty as Sorush is.

choices.text: Well, I am her Yasnapati, after all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* You're enjoying this, aren't you...

choices.text: Well, we've got a commission to complete.
The Rite of Chinvat?

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: This is a ritual performed by the Pari that will allow us to open a path through the darkness. It is said that the first Vijnanapati, Nagarjuna, and the Pari did just that.

response.speaker: Nasejuna
response.text: But we must first obtain the Great Songs and gather the power of Khvarena in order to initiate the Rite.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa? So this giant snake fella is also sealed here?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Yes, but it does not have a "sinful form." Perhaps it was merely unlucky to have been caught in the crossfire and sealed here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, maybe it's a good thing it's been sealed here. If not, it might just pop outta the ground and swallow us all in one go!

choices.text: I'll protect you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon knows that!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmm, you two certainly look like you get on well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course, we're the best of buddies!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But is it not also said that even constant companions would fail to notice if the other was spirited away by a sprite? These stories are quite common too, yes?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What are you talking about? {NICKNAME} would never do that.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hah, I merely jest. If you are bosom buddies, surely some idle jokes will not move you?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hehe. We shall soon reach the Vourukasha Oasis. Come, let us hurry.

choices.text: I don't think you'd be very good to eat, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon's not sure how to feel about that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa. The crystal here looks like...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could this be one of those Wenut that we've seen before? How did it get trapped here?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Hmm? So you call these children of an ancient dragon the Wenut?

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Still, it does not have a "sinful form." Perhaps it was merely unlucky to have been caught in the crossfire and sealed here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, maybe it's a good thing it's been sealed here. If not, it might just pop outta the ground and swallow us all in one go!

choices.text: I'll protect you, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, Paimon knows that!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hmm, you two certainly look like you get on well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Of course, we're the best of buddies!

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: But is it not also said that even constant companions would fail to notice if the other was spirited away by a sprite? These stories are quite common too, yes?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #What are you talking about? {NICKNAME} would never do that.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hah, I merely jest. If you are bosom buddies, surely some idle jokes will not move you?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Hehe. We shall soon reach the Vourukasha Oasis. Come, let us hurry.

choices.text: I don't think you'd be very good to eat, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um, Paimon's not sure how to feel about that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon didn't think there'd be such a huge patch of green on the other end of the mountain.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We were just in the desert, too. How strange!

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Impressive, is it not? It is our homeland, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The homeland of the Pari? So there'll be lots of other beings like you here, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, you know what? Paimon's not all that keen on going...

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Should you not be excited beyond words?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And the big tree stump over there looks like it's holding off the stuff oozing outta that big hole.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: That is the Harvisptokhm, the sacred form of the god that has granted us Pari life. It is not just some "large stump."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's a god? Well, we've seen other gods, but this is the first time we've seen one looking like that.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: That is because our go{RUBY#[S]Harvisptokhm}d cannot... be considered alive.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Five hundred years ago, our great god gave all to quell the power of the disaster afflicting this place.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: But she was stained with corruption, and could not be reborn in a purer plane. Thus, her divine consciousness continues to wander the mortal one.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Our great god left us with the sanctified Amrita, and the Lord of Verdure caused the Harvisptokhm to grow from that, thus anchoring our god to this realm.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: The Vourukasha Oasis has been nourished by the Amrita, and even the Khvarena that defends this earth gains its unending power by the grace of the Amrita.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But this god of yours doesn't look too well... She's been trying to hold out against the stuff coming out of that hole this entire time.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Her power maintains the seal over the dark hollow. I fear that the Sign has emerged here due to being attracted to her power.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: If it were not for the presence of the Harvisptokhm, the defilement surging forth from that hollow would have infected the entire world... But it is also due to performing this duty that the tree has deteriorated so much.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I do not believe that I could ever bear to be reduced to such a state.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: That is why I must leave a legacy of heroism behind for all to remember before it does happen...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, never mind that first. Let's go look for this Zurvan person, shall we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we get that Chaplet and fix the sky real quick, that might make your god feel all better too!

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Well, if it isn't Sorush. Such a rare guest.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: It has been a while... Elder Zurvan.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Elder? Well, if you call me that, then you should follow Pari norms and cease consorting with those humans whose hearts are heavy with their ulterior motives.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: I haven't gone against our norms. I have only made contact with humanity to find a way to extinguish the sky-fire, just as the divine bird did.

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: And is that why you have learned all that claptrap about sacrifice from the humans? We Pari care nothing for such foolishness.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Isn't it our duty as Pari to sacrifice ourselves in the battle against the defiling impurity?

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: Await the call of destiny, Sorush. Only humans rush in blindly.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: This destiny you speak of is a nebulous thing. I cannot simply be expected to sit and wait for it!

dialogues.speaker: Zurvan
dialogues.text: And that is precisely the danger. The Chaplet you seek contains the highest authority over Khvarena. In giving it to you, I may as well be handing the power of Khvarena over to those untrustworthy humans.

dialogues.speaker: Sorush
dialogues.text: Can't you just have more faith in me, Elder?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, you two... Looks like we're being left out here, aren't we?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Also, it seems like Sorush loses that cocky attitude of hers in front of Zurvan, huh? Hehe.

choices.text: She's probably just fond of weird roleplay.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And those Skeptics are all too happy to go along with her, huh?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Well then, little ones. You came with Sorush, yes? This is not a place that ordinary humans may visit lightly.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Let me see... Well, you certainly aren't from the Order of Skeptics. You seem to be outlanders, in fact.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Well, in matters of courtesy, I suppose you two shall introduce yourselves first. I don't ask humans for their names often, you know?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon's Paimon, and {M#he's}{F#she's} {NICKNAME}. We're...

choices.text: Adventurers who shuttle across Teyvat.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Adventurers... So you are travelers, then?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Well now, I do think I have seen a traveler much like you before.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: This is the forbidden land of the Pari, the paradise nourished by Amrita, the shrine at which we pay reverence to our great god.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Only heroes who have forged bonds with Pari and pilgrims who have come to genuflect before our god may enter.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: I shall take it that you are Sorush's companions, then. Hehe, it has been several hundred years since humans last visited our sea of flowers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, aren't there a ton of Skeptics living outside in the desert? Don't they know how to enter this place?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Hah! I shall not permit such discourteous folk to enter our hidden realm.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: In the past, we Pari did indeed fight alongside their ancestors. We even lived here together.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: But many years have passed, and folly has grown strong amongst them. Even the traditional rites have become utterly forgotten. None living amongst them now can forge a Laupa with a Pari.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: They should have been the ones to conduct the Rite of Ab-Zohr for the tree that suppresses the dark hollow, thus cleansing it of the filth that stained it.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Yes, the deterioration of the tree cannot be avoided, but if they had not neglected the Rite and caused the seal to weaken, this terrifying Sign would never have reappeared so soon.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: But human tradition is unreliable in this fashion. Compared to them, you outlanders, blank slates as you are, certainly seem more dependable.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's not sure if you're actually praising us or not, but we're here to...

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: I would guess that you are here about this sign in the sky. I doubt that anyone would notice our little nook if not for this great crisis.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... Well, we were commissioned to deal with this large hole, yeah.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Oh my, oh my, so it is as I guessed. It seems that even after so long, this short-lived race is as short-sighted as ever.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Still, if it were not that way, would you even need us Pari to act on your behalf?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: (Ugh, looks like Pari are just pretty nasty as a whole...)

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Regardless, since human heroes have again graced our secret garden, it seems the gears of destiny have begun to turn once more.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: And you seem to be an interesting human being, too. Ah, that takes me back... Once upon a time, I, too, traveled alongside humans as curious as you to quell a calamity.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Perhaps you really might equal their great deeds... Well then, it's decided. I shall give you a chance.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The two of you certainly seem more trustworthy than those blind and foolish Skeptics.

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: Elder, shouldn't you put your trust in me instead?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Well, as for that... You do know where Rashnu and Mihir are, right? Go bring them here. They should still be enjoying their beauty sleep right now.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: This will serve as proof of your trustworthiness, and I will be able to give the Chaplet to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, Paimon knows! So this is the kind of seal that everyone needs to get together to break, and then we can get the Chaplet, right?

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Ah, such impoverished imagination.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: The Chaplet can be given to you at any time. But to solve the issue of the Sign of Apaosha, we will need their strength.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Sorush alone will not be able to open the path through the dark hollow, not even with the Chaplet. This, perhaps, is another example of the Rule of Three...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't really know what you're saying, but as long as we can get the Chaplet, it's fine.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: #Indeed, {NICKNAME}, Paimon. Do help Sorush out, alright?

response.speaker: Sorush
response.text: I don't need help...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ahaha, you're not very honest, Sorush. But since your elder's said so, guess you've just gotta listen to us!

choices.text: I am Sorush's Yasnapati.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: Her Yasnapati? ... How interesting.

response.speaker: Zurvan
response.text: She might have had a little misunderstanding somewhere, though. Haha.

choices.text: Perhaps she has other hidden facets to her person...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a scary thought!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Found it, found it! Paimon wonders what it is...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Aw, come on, this is no treasure. It's just some tattered old drum!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We don't know what it could be used for, either.

choices.text: If we brought this one back to the Akademiya...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right, they might want to hear more about something we found in the desert.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's not all that interested in this studying stuff, but if we can make a little this and that off their budget, why not, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm, hold on. There's a note over there at the side. It might just hold some clues!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let Paimon see... Huh. This seems to have been left by an adventurer.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "The Sign of Apaosha"... Uh, Paimon's not super sure what this guy's talking about, but he sure is irresponsible, leaving a commission unfinished just because it's hard!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But since that's how things are, let's hand this drum over to Katheryne and let her reassign someone to complete... whatever commission this was.

choices.text: Let's say we brought this back to the Grand Bazaar...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! Maybe the people at the Theater could make use of this. But wouldn't they already have a lot of these instruments there already?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But y'know, it's not as if Paimon really knows the difference between drum types or anything.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: Then I shall leave the matter of the Twin-Horned Chaplet to you. I have some leftover work to take care of.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: I believe that all people, no matter who they are, will submit to you and the Envoy's awesome glory.

dialogues.speaker: Nasejuna
dialogues.text: When we have each done what we must, let us meet at the campsite upon the Temir Mountains.
